items.text: palettes. The Color panel opens on the palette: one strip of its colors in order (Ink 1, Ink 2, mix, Touch, Ground, Arrows, Pattern); tap one to edit it below. Its name opens the palettes, eight from the studio and your own: a tap wears one

Follows: a color can be tied to another, the complement of Ink 1, a deep or pale version, lighter, darker, warmer, cooler; change that one and the tied ones move with it. One color, related is a palette made this way
Save palette keeps the colors and their ties; a scene saved with a palette points at it, so changing the palette changes every scene that uses it
the two particle colors are Ink 1 and Ink 2, and their mix is Ink mix: particles draw lines or dots, and a material can borrow either ink

In time follows the tempo: the inks swap on each beat or each bar of the same tempo as Autoplay and the metronome (tapped, or the beat that plays); Own sets seconds of your own. In time is last, right above its settings
in the Color panel the color circle is the color wheel: tap it for your device's picker; the on / off is a toggle on one line
dragging the speaker sideways keeps the button as it is: the ring around it shows the volume, as the dice show theirs; no fill, no number
Lapping waves is softer: little sloshes that gurgle as they fall back, no knocks
beds fade: switching or stopping a water bed or a pack's bed sound fades it down over about two seconds while the next one rises; a bed that keeps playing is left alone
Stream is a little bubbling brook now; the old sound is kept and named for what it is, Garden hose; and a new bed, Lapping waves: tiny waves at a lakeshore, against a dock and the stones
the Color panel says Color · and what it colors (Color · Ground); Lines and Second are Line 1 and Line 2, Mix is Line mix
in the Color panel the small square says wheel (your device's color picker), the switch says what it is and whether it's on (Line 1 on), and How it works (i) explains each element
the Color panel has ‹ › to the next panel and its ring in its band
drag the speaker left or right for the volume, as the dice do; down and up open its shelf and panel as before
stepping from one panel to the next with ‹ ›, a pinned ring goes along: it becomes the next panel's ring, in the same place
a ring opened from a panel stays on the stage when the panel closes, as long as it is pinned; unpinned, it goes with the panel

more than one ring. On a computer with room, a double tap while a ring is pinned opens another; the pinned one stays, a step back, and a touch takes it in hand again. Settings › Another ring: With room, Always or Never
a double tap on the stage brings back the last ring you opened there; a ring opened from a panel's ring button belongs to that panel and doesn't change it
